summary: Extends BGP-4 so it can carry routing information for network protocols other than IPv4, such as IPv6 and VPN address families. The extensions are backward compatible, so upgraded routers still interoperate with older ones.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4760 extends BGP-4 so it can advertise routes for network-layer protocols beyond IPv4. It adds separate messages for reachable routes and withdrawals, while allowing routers that lack the extension to ignore those additions.

questions: how does bgp carry ipv6 routes
subtitle: How BGP carries routes for different network-layer protocols in a backward-compatible way.

tldr.problem: BGP-4 ties its next-hop and route-prefix information to IPv4. It needs a way to describe routes for other network-layer protocols too.
tldr.mechanism: MP_REACH_NLRI carries reachable routes with their address-family identifiers and next hop. MP_UNREACH_NLRI carries withdrawals, and BGP capability advertisements let peers agree which address-family pairs they support.
tldr.outcome: Peers that do not support the optional, non-transitive attributes ignore them. RFC 4760 obsoletes RFC 2858 and is updated by RFC 7606.

today: RFC 4760 is a Draft Standard that obsoletes RFC 2858. It is updated by RFC 7606.

sections.title: Why BGP Needs Multiprotocol Support
sections.content:
BGP-4 carries three IPv4-specific items: the NEXT_HOP attribute, the AGGREGATOR attribute, and Network Layer Reachability Information (NLRI) written as IPv4 prefixes. RFC 4760 adds a way to associate a network-layer protocol with both the next-hop information and the routes.

The protocol uses an Address Family Identifier (AFI) together with a Subsequent Address Family Identifier (SAFI). This pair identifies the network-layer protocol and the meaning of the route information.
sections.plainLanguage: Older BGP route messages describe IPv4 addresses. The RFC adds labels so a route and its next hop can be understood for another network-layer protocol.

sections.title: Reachable Routes and Withdrawals
sections.content:
MP_REACH_NLRI (Type Code 14) advertises feasible routes and the next-hop network address for them. Its fields include the AFI, SAFI, next-hop length and address, a reserved octet, and NLRI. The reserved octet MUST be set to zero and SHOULD be ignored when received.

MP_UNREACH_NLRI (Type Code 15) withdraws routes and carries an AFI, SAFI, and withdrawn NLRI. It does not need any other path attributes. Both attributes are optional and non-transitive, so a speaker without this extension ignores them and does not pass them on.

An UPDATE containing MP_REACH_NLRI MUST also contain ORIGIN and AS_PATH; an IBGP UPDATE of this kind MUST also contain LOCAL_PREF. The RFC also says not to repeat the same prefix for one AFI and SAFI across multiple route fields in an UPDATE.
sections.plainLanguage: One attribute lists routes that can be reached and the next hop to use. A second lists routes being withdrawn; older routers can ignore both attributes.

sections.title: Route Prefixes and SAFI Values
sections.content:
Each NLRI entry is a length and a prefix. Length gives the number of significant prefix bits; zero means a prefix matching every address in that address family. The prefix is padded with trailing bits to end on an octet boundary, and those trailing bits have no meaning.

This RFC assigns SAFI 1 to NLRI used for unicast forwarding and SAFI 2 to NLRI used for multicast forwarding. An implementation may support all, some, or none of the SAFI values defined here.
sections.plainLanguage: A route entry says how many prefix bits matter and then gives those bits. SAFI says whether the route information is for unicast or multicast forwarding.

sections.title: Agreeing on Address Families
sections.content:
A BGP speaker SHOULD use capability advertisement to learn whether a peer supports the multiprotocol extension. The capability has Code 1 and Length 4; its value contains a 16-bit AFI, a reserved octet, and an 8-bit SAFI. The sender SHOULD set the reserved octet to zero, and the receiver SHOULD ignore it.

Speakers that support multiple AFI and SAFI pairs include multiple capabilities. For routing information to flow in both directions for a pair, each speaker MUST advertise support for that pair to the other.
sections.plainLanguage: Before using an address-family pair, each router tells its peer which pairs it supports. Both routers must advertise the same pair for routes to flow in both directions.

sections.title: Handling an Incorrect Attribute
sections.content:
If a speaker decides an MP_REACH_NLRI or MP_UNREACH_NLRI attribute is incorrect, it MUST delete routes learned from that neighbor for the same AFI and SAFI. For the rest of that BGP session, it SHOULD ignore later routes with that pair.

The speaker MAY end the session. If it does, it SHOULD send a Notification indicating UPDATE Message Error and Optional Attribute Error.
sections.plainLanguage: If a router finds a bad attribute, it removes routes for that address-family pair from that neighbor. It may also end the BGP session.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that these extensions do not change the security issues already present in BGP. It adds no separate security mechanism or security claim for the multiprotocol attributes.
sections.plainLanguage: The extension leaves BGP's existing security issues unchanged. The RFC does not define a new security mechanism here.
